findings.issue: Security audit says 'reaction routes use anon client — P0 cross-tenant access'. Full RBAC feature prompt says 'implement channel-level role overrides'. These contradict: reaction routes just need middleware membership check (fix exists: requireChannelAccess), not full RBAC redesign (multi-sprint effort). Cross-referencing could lead to over-engineering.
findings.impact: Implementing full RBAC to fix reaction routes wastes ~3 sprints for a 1-hour fix.
findings.fix: Fix reaction routes independently with requireChannelAccess middleware. Channel-level RBAC overrides are a separate effort with different scope and justification.

findings.issue: Environment audit says 'API subdomain DNS unused, remove'. Infra audit says 'API subdomain DNS reserved for future split-domain architecture'. Direct contradiction on whether to keep or delete the DNS record.
findings.impact: Deleting DNS record could block future architecture evolution. Keeping it maintains unused infra indefinitely.
findings.fix: Keep DNS record but add comment: 'Reserved for future split-domain (API <-> web) architecture. Do not delete without architect approval.' Defer removal decision.

findings.issue: 'Message search uses anon client' rated P0 in security audit (cross-tenant leak) but P1 in API contract audit (incorrect client type). Same code, same impact — different severity.
findings.impact: Severity inconsistency undermines prioritization. P0 items get immediate attention, P1 items get deferred.
findings.fix: Normalize to P0: anon client means auth.uid() is NULL, SECURITY INVOKER function has no user context — cross-tenant data leak is possible. All instances of anon client usage in data-access code are P0.

findings.issue: 'No git tags or semver releases' rated P2 in rollback audit but P3 in platform audit. Both agree it's missing but disagree on severity by one level.
findings.impact: Minor but affects whether item gets prioritized in current sprint vs backlog.
findings.fix: Normalize to P3: git tags are best practice but SHA-based Docker image tags provide production traceability. Git tags are nice-to-have, not blocking.

findings.issue: UX audit says 'theme toggle has no transition animation = P2'. Performance audit says 'client-side theme flash (FOUT) = P1'. Both about theme but different aspects: SSR hydration fix (P1) vs CSS animation (P2). Risk of conflating them into one ticket.
findings.impact: SSR theme flash is a user-facing defect. CSS transition is a nice-to-have. Conflating them would block the quick fix with the aesthetic item.
findings.fix: Keep separate: (P1) SSR-safe theme hydration via cookie-based initial theme, (P2) CSS transition on theme switch color properties. Different scopes, different fixes.

findings.issue: Feature prompts sequence: Phase 1 = core features (threads, mentions, RBAC, webhooks, search, editor). Platform readiness says 'regenerate types and add worker first'. Infrastructure audit says 'deploy Redis first'. Three different sequences for the same work.
findings.impact: Feature implementation without infrastructure prerequisites will hit Redis/worker gaps. Types won't match schema after migrations.
findings.fix: Resequence to reconciled order: Phase 0 = infra hardening (Redis, worker, types regeneration), Phase 1 = security fixes, Phase 2 = core features, Phase 3 = frontend depth, Phase 4 = media/UX.

findings.issue: One audit says 'add OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing'. Observability audit says 'request IDs sufficient at current scale, OTEL overengineering'. Direct contradiction on telemetry strategy.
findings.impact: Contradictory recommendations waste effort on wrong solution.
findings.fix: Defer OTEL. Implement structured request IDs with log shipping (Papertrail/Loki). Re-evaluate OTEL when scaling beyond 5 API instances. Document decision.

findings.issue: 'TypeScript types out of sync with schema' appears in database audit, platform readiness, and evolution ultra — three identical findings with same fix (regenerate supabase types).
findings.impact: Counted 3x overstating effort. Real fix is one command: npx supabase gen types typescript --local > packages/db/src/types.ts
findings.fix: Consolidate to one finding with CI drift check: add supabase gen types to validate.yml and fail if types are out of sync.

findings.issue: 'No i18n support' flagged P3 in accessibility audit but codebase has no internationalization requirements documented. Assumption may not be valid if i18n is intentionally out of scope.
findings.impact: Finding may not be actionable. Effort spent on i18n infrastructure may be wasted.
findings.fix: Document scope decision: 'i18n not planned for MVP. All UI text in English. Re-evaluate if non-English users exceed 20%.' Remove i18n findings if out of scope.

findings.issue: 'Add k6 load testing to CI' recommended by test expansion prompt but Redis not deployed yet — k6 tests against single-instance API won't represent production behavior with multiple instances and Redis.
findings.impact: Load test results from single-instance setup are not representative of production behavior.
findings.fix: Defer full load tests until multi-instance deployment with Redis is possible. Add unit-level performance benchmarks in the meantime.
